newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler works council refuses overtime in row.
newsitem.headline: Daimler works council refuses overtime in row.

text.p: The works council at Daimler-Benz AG said on Wednesday that it would refuse overtime work in a bitter row with the German industrial group which said it would cut sick pay benefits.

Daimler said on Tuesday it would implement controversial new legislation to cut sick pay to 80 percent from Oct 1 despite unions and some leading politicians saying companies like Daimler had no right to make such cutbacks so quickly.
Daimler works council chairman Karl Feuerstein told journalists that the council board had voted in favour of not working overtime shifts.
At plants with weekend and overtime shifts written into contracts, he said he did not expect employees to show up for work.

Unions and some top politicians said Daimler had no right to make the sickpay cutback, and that the bill passed by parliament earlier this month was not meant to apply to existing contracts, only future ones.

But Daimler and other industrial leaders have taken a sharply different view and intend to use the legislation, which is part of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's programme to boost sagging unemployment, to reopen talks with unions on cutting costs.
